selected.lesson_subject: IPv6 PCP MAP-controlled DNAT46 mappings in NAT64 deployments
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: PCP MAP request creates a time-bounded inbound mapping in a FortiGate PCP pool with NAT46 enabled; DNAT46 maps an IPv4 service endpoint to an IPv6 client address.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IPv6 client -> PCP MAP request -> PCP server pool validates client prefix/opcode/lifetime -> mapping installed -> IPv4 service packet hits NAT46 policy -> DNAT46 mapping translates destination -> reply uses mapping until lifetime expiry/recycle.
selected.failure_class: PCP request rejected, mapping not created/expired, wrong pool/policy binding, NAT46 disabled or address-family mismatch.
selected.evidence_pattern: PCP mapping table/pool state, request opcode and lifetime, policy hit/session tuple, packet capture on IPv6 client and IPv4 service sides; each proves a different stage.
selected.remediation_path: Validate client6-prefix, external address/port range, allowed MAP opcode, lifetime bounds, NAT46 enablement, PCP inbound mode and pool on the matching NAT46 firewall policy; retest mapping then data path.
selected.question_fingerprint: Differentiate PCP control-plane MAP success from actual DNAT46 data-plane policy/session success.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: IPv6 client -> PCP control request -> FortiGate PCP pool -> NAT46/DNAT46 policy -> IPv4 server; separate control and data paths.
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: prefix delegation assigns prefixes to downstream routers; PCP creates per-client port/address mappings and DNAT46 translations. Different protocol, state, transaction, evidence and remediation.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiGuard package version pinning and controlled downgrade semantics
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiManager acting as FortiGuard server can hold a selected package object version as the maximum version it will provide; administrators separately choose whether existing devices are downgraded.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Administrator chooses To Be Deployed Version -> FortiManager retains package revisions (default maximum 20) -> managed FortiGate requests package update -> FortiManager serves pinned version -> if device already has newer version, explicit Just Set Preferred Version or Downgrade decision controls state transition.
selected.failure_class: Unexpected signature/application package drift, pinned version not available due retention, or accidental downgrade during version pinning.
selected.evidence_pattern: Receive Status package version table, current device package version, selected To Be Deployed Version, device update result and actual package version on FortiGate.
selected.remediation_path: Select package under FortiGuard > Packages > Receive Status; distinguish holding a ceiling from forcing rollback; verify the chosen version is retained and test a representative device before broad rollout.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish version ceiling from immediate rollback and infer the effect on devices already running newer package versions.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Admin -> FortiManager package repository/version selector -> FortiGate update request -> pinned response; separate hold-only and downgrade branches.
selected.closest_historical_match: Policy Blocks reusable rule sets and installation-target boundaries (2026-10-27)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: Policy Blocks compose configuration objects; this feature controls FortiGuard package version delivery and rollback semantics. Different objects, control plane and failure evidence.

selected.lesson_subject: Energy-efficient Ethernet low-power timing and LLDP 802.3 EEE negotiation
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: EEE allows supported twisted-pair copper PHYs to enter low-power idle during quiet periods and return to normal operation when frames arrive; LLDP 802.3 EEE TLV advertises EEE capability/configuration.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Port auto-negotiates supported speed -> PHY and link partner negotiate EEE capability/timing -> idle periods enter low-power state -> wake timing restores normal signaling -> LLDP profile can advertise EEE configuration.
selected.failure_class: EEE absent due forced speed, unsupported SFP/QSFP medium, peer capability mismatch, LLDP TLV not enabled, or wake timing interoperability issue.
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose switch physical-ports eee-status, physical port speed/auto-negotiation state, LLDP profile 802.3 TLV and peer LLDP data; distinguish EEE support from actual negotiated operation.
selected.remediation_path: Use auto-negotiation on supported copper port, verify peer EEE support, exclude SFP/QSFP, configure LLDP 802.3 eee-config TLV, inspect EEE status and test link wake under load.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish EEE capability advertisement from negotiated low-power operation and identify unsupported media/forced-speed constraints.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiSwitch copper PHY <-> peer PHY with LLDP EEE TLV side channel and sleep/wake timing state machine.
selected.closest_historical_match: Dynamic VLAN pruning GVRP state and ISL trunk membership (2026-10-28)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: VLAN membership pruning is a control-plane membership mechanism; EEE is PHY low-power negotiation/timing. Different layer and evidence.

selected.lesson_subject: RADIUS authentication survivability cache for 802.1X enterprise SSIDs
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS wireless controller caches credentials/authorization data for previously authenticated 802.1X clients and can locally reauthenticate them during RADIUS outage for a bounded interval.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client authenticates successfully to RADIUS -> required cache attributes and server certificates are present -> FortiGate stores survivability record -> RADIUS becomes unreachable -> reconnect uses cached credential/authorization -> timeout expires -> client is no longer authorized -> RADIUS recovery restores normal server-backed auth.
selected.failure_class: Client cannot be cached due missing Fortinet-AS-Credential-Hash/Cisco AVPair, missing CA/server cert, timeout expiry, unsupported EAP mode or SSID option disabled.
selected.evidence_pattern: diagnose wpa wpad radius-auth-surviv-cache <SSID>, cache_cnt/expiration/VLAN/EAP type, online station table and server reachability; RADIUS outage alone does not prove local cache eligibility.
selected.remediation_path: Configure RADIUS server to return credential hash attribute for EAP-PEAP, import trusted CA and RADIUS server certificate, set wifi-ca-certificate/wifi-certificate, enable survivability and bounded interval on VAP, test reconnect during controlled outage.
selected.question_fingerprint: Separate ordinary RADIUS server failure from missing cache prerequisites and determine what the expiry timer means for authorization.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: 802.1X client -> FortiAP -> FortiGate wireless controller -> RADIUS server; local cache branch on RADIUS outage with timeout expiry.
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: EST/SCEP bootstraps client certificates; survivability caches previously validated RADIUS credential state for bounded outage reauthentication. Different transaction.

selected.lesson_subject: Endpoint compliance scan scheduling and host-health state persistence
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC records each Agent, System and Admin scan separately; the currently applicable Agent scan is policy-selected, while failed Admin/System scans can continue to gate access after an Agent policy changes.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Endpoint becomes eligible under compliance policy -> agent scan runs -> result stored in Host Health and history -> policy may select a different Agent scan -> prior Agent result for superseded scan stops governing current policy, but Admin/System failures remain independent access gates.
selected.failure_class: Host remains At Risk after policy change because Admin/System scan failed, current Agent scan is still failed, rescan was not queued/completed, or stale result is misinterpreted.
selected.evidence_pattern: Users & Hosts > Hosts > Host Properties > Health; scan type/name/status/current-agent highlight; Show History timestamps and scan detail; ReScan queue result.
selected.remediation_path: Identify which scan type is blocking access; verify currently applied Agent scan; inspect Admin/System state separately; queue ReScan and confirm endpoint contact; change scan configuration with awareness that prior failures are not retroactively rewritten.
selected.question_fingerprint: Determine whether a host is blocked by the current Agent scan or an independent Admin/System scan after policy change.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Endpoint -> compliance policy -> Agent scan A/B -> Host Health state; parallel Admin and System gates feed network access decision.
selected.closest_historical_match: Windows AV compliance using Security-Center provider (2026-11-11)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: Windows AV provider lesson is one scan's evidence source; this lesson covers cross-scan state precedence, persistence and policy-change semantics.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiNAC-F event export pipeline: receiver types, event mapping and internal/external persistence
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiNAC-F separates receiver definitions from per-event logging mode; events can be internal, external, or both and are serialized as Syslog CSV/CEF, SNMP traps or FortiAnalyzer OFTP.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Create receiver in System Communication > Log Receivers -> select protocol/address/port/facility/security string -> map event in Event Management -> event is persisted internally and/or sent externally -> downstream collector parses event type, severity, entity and message fields.
selected.failure_class: Event generated but absent externally because event mapping is disabled/wrong, receiver/protocol/port is incorrect, format/receiver is incompatible, or external-only mode loses internal forensic copy.
selected.evidence_pattern: Event Management Log state, receiver definition, packet capture to receiver, Syslog/SNMP payload, internal event record and downstream receipt; a database event alone does not prove external forwarding.
selected.remediation_path: Verify receiver address/type/port and event mapping; choose Internal & External when local forensic history is required; capture UDP/TCP receiver traffic and validate format fields at collector; avoid assuming External means both.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish event generation, internal persistence and remote delivery; identify the evidence needed at each boundary.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Event producer -> event mapping branch -> internal event DB and/or external receiver -> Syslog/SNMP/OFTP collector.
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: host-learning traps are inbound switch-to-NAC topology events; this is outbound NAC event export and persistence selection.

selected.lesson_subject: EAP-TTLS/PAP 2FA: tunneled credential flow, token carriage and challenge limitation
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: EAP-TTLS establishes a TLS tunnel to the RADIUS authentication server and carries an inner method such as PAP; challenge-based EAP-TTLS 2FA behavior is version-dependent, with older versions requiring password+OTP concatenation.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: IKEv2/802.1X client starts EAP -> RADIUS EAP server certificate is validated -> TLS tunnel established -> inner PAP credentials are validated against local/remote identity source -> FortiToken factor is checked according to version-supported flow -> Access-Accept/Reject returns to NAS.
selected.failure_class: Password validates but 2FA remains partial/expecting token; challenge cannot be presented inside TTLS flow, wrong client EAP support, untrusted server certificate, or incompatible FortiAuthenticator/FortiClient/FortiOS versions.
selected.evidence_pattern: RADIUS log shows Remote LDAP user password authenticated, expecting FortiToken, then EAP authentication failed due to missing token; EAP-TTLS Access-Reject; client does not display token prompt.
selected.remediation_path: Verify client and server EAP-TTLS support and versions; trust server certificate; check whether 8.0.4+ behavior applies; on versions requiring it use supported password+OTP concatenation; do not use email/SMS OTP where the second factor cannot be received before password submission.
selected.question_fingerprint: Identify why password success followed by 'expecting FortiToken' still results in Access-Reject, and choose a version-appropriate token carriage method.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: FortiClient EAP initiator -> TLS tunnel to FortiAuthenticator RADIUS -> inner PAP -> LDAP/local password validation -> FortiToken factor -> RADIUS response.
selected.closest_historical_match: RADIUS policy selection, top-down precedence, local EAP versus proxy (2026-10-30)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: policy selection decides which authentication policy handles the request; this lesson covers TTLS tunnel termination, inner PAP and 2FA token carriage/version constraints.

selected.lesson_subject: FortiPAM glass-breaking mode: emergency secret access expansion, audit and alert controls
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: A role permission can allow a user to enter glass-breaking mode, temporarily extending access beyond normal per-secret/folder permissions to all secrets for exceptional recovery situations.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Admin role grants Enter Glass Breaking Mode -> authorized operator activates mode during exceptional outage -> access scope expands to all secrets -> event trigger/audit log records activation -> email alert can notify reviewers -> operator exits mode and access returns to normal role/secret permissions.
selected.failure_class: Emergency operator cannot activate due missing role permission, broad access is left active too long, activation is not alerted/audited, or maintenance mode is confused with glass-breaking mode.
selected.evidence_pattern: Role Admin Settings permission, Glass Breaking Activated trigger, Events/Logs entry and email alert; maintenance mode is a separate process-suspension control.
selected.remediation_path: Restrict the permission to a small emergency-admin role, configure Glass Breaking Activated trigger and alert recipients, rehearse controlled activation/deactivation, review event logs and confirm normal secret ACLs apply after exit.
selected.question_fingerprint: Differentiate temporary all-secret emergency access from maintenance mode and ordinary secret approval/checkout.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Normal RBAC/secret ACL -> emergency glass-breaking activation -> expanded secret scope -> trigger/audit/alert -> deactivation -> normal ACL restored.
selected.closest_historical_match: Approval revocation as a live session-control action (2026-10-30)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: approval revocation terminates/controls one authorized session; glass breaking is a role-gated emergency scope expansion across all secrets with separate audit/alert lifecycle.

selected.lesson_subject: HTTP/3 QUIC inspection actions in security profile groups
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiSASE can inspect HTTP/3 over QUIC for agent and edge-device traffic through SSL inspection settings; policy offers Inspect, Bypass or Block actions and proxy-policy traffic has a separate constraint.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Client sends QUIC over UDP/443 -> security profile group selects HTTP/3 action -> Inspect passes traffic to inspection features; Bypass permits without inspection; Block drops QUIC so browser commonly falls back to HTTP/2 over TLS/TCP -> proxy-user path may require browser QUIC disablement.
selected.failure_class: Security profile does not inspect HTTP/3, traffic bypasses inspection, proxy policy cannot apply same HTTP/3 setting, or QUIC block fails to cause expected fallback.
selected.evidence_pattern: Security profile group SSL inspection method, HTTP/3 action, endpoint UDP/443 capture, browser protocol result and inspection logs; browser fallback does not prove deep inspection occurred.
selected.remediation_path: Choose Certificate or Deep inspection before configuring HTTP/3 action; scope the profile to agent/edge traffic; for proxy users block QUIC at browser/endpoint or policy layer and verify HTTP/2 fallback; test inspect/bypass/block separately.
selected.question_fingerprint: Distinguish Inspect from Bypass and Block, and recognize that proxy-policy traffic is not governed by the agent/edge HTTP/3 action.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Agent/edge QUIC UDP443 -> security profile group -> Inspect/Bypass/Block branches; proxy-user browser QUIC block -> HTTP/2 fallback.
selected.closest_historical_match: Secure Browser extension profiles and browser-side controls (2026-11-11)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: Secure Browser controls browser extension/identity behavior; HTTP/3 inspection is transport/protocol-specific security inspection and QUIC fallback.

selected.lesson_subject: IPv6 segmentation across a shared ADVPN overlay using VRF route isolation
selected.feature_mechanism_fingerprint: FortiOS supports multiple IPv6 VRF overlay networks over a single ADVPN overlay, allowing branches to reuse the same prefixes while keeping route tables and shortcut reachability isolated.
selected.workflow_transaction_fingerprint: Spoke attaches IPv6 subnets to VRF-specific overlay interfaces -> BGP VPNv6 route exchange/route-reflector client advertises VRF routes -> hub and spoke maintain per-VRF route tables -> ADVPN shortcut forms within the matching VRF -> shared tunnel transport carries isolated tenant traffic without cross-VRF route mixing.
selected.failure_class: IPv6 route not imported/advertised, wrong VRF/interface binding, route-reflector/additional-path settings incomplete, shortcut not established, or overlapping prefixes leak across VRF boundary.
selected.evidence_pattern: Per-VRF IPv6 routing table, BGP VPNv6 received/advertised routes, neighbor-group RR/activate/additional-path settings, shortcut tunnel state and packet capture showing VRF interface/route selection.
selected.remediation_path: Validate VRF assignment on each overlay interface, VPNv6 activation and route-reflector-client settings, additional-path configuration where used, per-VRF prefix advertisements and shortcut formation; test same-prefix isolation between tenants.
selected.question_fingerprint: Determine why shared ADVPN transport does not imply shared routing, and isolate missing VPNv6 route reflection from a shortcut/underlay problem.
selected.diagram_topology_layout_fingerprint: Two tenants/VRFs with overlapping IPv6 prefixes -> shared ADVPN hub/overlay -> VPNv6 route reflection -> per-VRF shortcuts and isolated route tables.
selected.closest_historical_match: Remote-health-check BGP route suppression across dual hubs (2026-11-02)
selected.uniqueness_decision: PASS: remote-health-check suppresses hub routes on dead overlays; this lesson isolates IPv6 tenants by VRF over one shared ADVPN transport. Different routing objective and state.
